summary: K16 SHIPPED AND IT CATCHES THE DEFECT THAT MOTIVATED IT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE ROUND, AND THE SUITE IS RED IN TWO PLACES ON PURPOSE. K16 -- tests/test_contract.py::check_k16_verdicts_follow_their_printed_pair -- reads a Gate's VERDICT against the (value vs threshold) pair Gate.line prints beside it, which nothing in this tree had ever done. THE RULE, and it is the largest one I could make sound: recover the boolean expression that decides `fired` (a Compare, a local name assigned once, a bool() of either, or a call to a src/spine/derive.py function that is one `return` over its own parameters, unfolded by substitution); examine the Gate only when its printed pair IS one of that expression's comparison clauses (value renders the left operand, threshold the right); and report it when the verdict turns on MORE clauses than the pair shows, with no reason on the line and no clause settled by `reachable=` or by an enclosing branch that holds it true. CALIBRATION, over every commit in this repository that carries a src/ directory -- 73 trees, a47c569 through 6237858 -- plus the working tree: the rule reports src/fabric/api.py's fab.cull_gate at all 34 trees since d8afb7b wrote it, ONE true instance per tree, and NOTHING ELSE at any tree, ever. At each of the eight archived commits in my brief the examined population is 8, TRUE=1, FALSE ALARMS=0. WHAT I LEFT OUT, and it is printed on the check's own report line and not only here: the DIRECTION of the comparison (Gate.line prints no operator, so '(0.500 vs 0.45)' cannot say >= from <, and 25 of the resolved verdicts are `>` but one is `<` and one is `!=` -- the naive 'fired implies value >= threshold' rule would call those two defects); a threshold that spells its own relation in prose (25 are a bare string, 23 an f-string, and src/fabric/api.py's fab.discover is `discovered > 0` against threshold f'cosine distance > {discover}', where the `>` in the text is about a different quantity -- that one gate is why I did not read the operator out of the text); a clause not written as a comparison; and whether an exempting reason NAMES the clause its pair omits. THE RED IS THE CORRECT STATE. K16's single finding is src/fabric/api.py, which I do not own; O13's three are src/spine/assemble.py plus the two lines docs/03_WIRING.md generates from it, which I do not own either. Both repairs are in `unfinished`, anchored on text, and BOTH ARE VERIFIED: with them applied to a scratch mirror the whole suite is green (contract 16 checks + 77 cases 0 failing, ownership 13 + 43 0 failing, and the other five files unmoved). ITEM 4, DECIDED: I TOOK the O13 widening, WITH i_docs' clause. h_docs' version as written is NOT a widening and I reproduced that -- it examines 6 and DROPS src/fabric/api.py's citation of spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_windows, which O13 examines today across the gap ': '. With the clause it examines 7, a true superset of today's 3, the same 3 findings, and zero false alarms. ITEM 3: all five re-verified before touching anything; four stand and are fixed, and the subscripted-value one is WRONG AS FILED -- ast.unparse normalises string literals to single quotes, so the example it names produces a perfectly well-formed suggestion. I fixed the real, narrower collision instead and said so in the code. ONE HAND-OFF ITEM I ALMOST FILED IS STALE: i_fab-derive's src/spine/derive.py docstring finding is already repaired in the tree by another agent this round, which I found by running the arithmetic against the current file instead of relaying the report. ONE CORRECTION TO MY OWN BRIEF: fab.cull_gate does not print a contradicting pair 'on every run'. It needs FAB_N0 <= 2 AND the occupancy at or above FAB_PRESSURE -- four rows of the six I ran. At the shipped defaults it prints 'FIRED (2048/4096=0.500 vs 0.45)', which agrees.

K16 checks that the arithmetic can produce the verdict. findings.symbol: tests/test_contract.py -- rule 5's suggested-remedy string on a subscripted `value=` (item 3, third sub-item)
findings.detail: WRONG AS FILED, AND I FIXED THE REAL, NARROWER THING INSTEAD. The report says the suggestion is malformed 'if a Gate's `value=` ever unparses to something containing a double quote (a subscript such as st.counters[\"opt.x\"])' and proposes falling back whenever a quote OF EITHER KIND appears. Both halves are wrong: `ast.unparse` NORMALISES string literals to single quotes, so st.counters[\"opt.x\"] comes back as st.counters['opt.x'] and sits inside f\"...\" perfectly well on Python 3.11 -- the cited example produces a well-formed suggestion, and the proposed guard would drop the echo for it. A double quote appears in unparse's output ONLY when the literal itself contains an apostrophe, and then the value carries BOTH quote characters and no single-line f-string can wrap it at all (I tried choosing the outer quote to clear the inner one and the result still fails to compile). SHIPPED: the echo is dropped and the expression named in words when and only when the unparsed value contains a double quote, with a self-test case that takes the branch -- because a guard nothing has tripped is the class this repository has sixty records of. Rule 5's live population is 4 (src/ckpt/api.py:446 `every`, src/opt/api.py:1930 `shift_warm`, :1845 and :1864 `damp`), every one a bare local name, so nothing in src/ reaches either branch's difference.

A span may be SINGLE-quoted; the gap may be a CLAUSE ending in a verb inside 120 characters (either that form or the whole-gap form, which is i_docs' clause) and may not cross a sentence boundary; a paren pair no longer disqualifies a span, which instead has to run to eight words; and `::<module>` resolves against the cited FILE.
